page: Microsoft Azure D8ls_v7 is an x86_64 architecture server instance belonging to the Dlsv7 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 8 dedicated vCPUs mapped from 4 physical Intel Xeon 6973P-C cores, operating at a clock speed of 4.2 GHz. The processor includes a 480 MB L3 cache, 2 MB L2 cache, and 48 KB L1d cache. Memory capacity is constrained to 16.0 GB, yielding a low memory-to-core ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. This instance does not include local storage or bundled GPUs, but it is Premium Storage capable.

Benchmark data indicates average performance across most standard compute and memory operations. The single-core stress-ng CPU performance is recorded at 2220.68, while the multi-core score reaches 9233.86. Single-threaded gzip compression and bzip3 decompression show strong performance at 36.07 GB/sec and 14.99 GB/sec respectively. Memory bandwidth tests show 684.86 GB/sec for cached small-block reads, dropping to 85.56 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads, and 39.38 GB/sec for large-block writes. For lightweight machine learning workloads, the server achieves a strong text generation speed of 266.79 tokens/sec on a small 135M LLM model, though medium 7B model generation drops to an average of 10.08 tokens/sec.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the D8ls_v7 offers a compute-dense profile with dedicated Intel Xeon cores at a lower memory allocation, making it a resource-efficient option for CPU-bound tasks that do not require large memory footprints. The primary tradeoff is the low memory density of 2.0 GB per vCPU, which limits its suitability for memory-intensive databases or massive datasets. The server is best suited for workloads such as static web serving, single-threaded compression tasks, lightweight containerized applications, and basic computational tasks.
